evidence_candidates.claim: AI Agent Configuration exposes capabilities, tools, data sources, credentials, prompts and behavioural settings that adversaries may acquire to map or attack an agent deployment.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Complements configuration secrecy, agent inventory and credential governance.

evidence_candidates.claim: AI Agent Tools are a distinct AI supply-chain target because they can provide broad access and permissions through connected services, data sources and execution capabilities.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Candidate complement for supply-chain, third-party tool and permission notes.

evidence_candidates.claim: A poisoned AI agent tool may alter definitions or runtime responses, invoke additional tools, execute malicious logic or create unauthorised access.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Directly extends tool invocation, prompt injection and supply-chain risk coverage.

evidence_candidates.claim: AI Agent Tool Invocation describes adversarial use of an agent's tool interface as an execution and access path.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Cross-reference to existing human-in-the-loop and least-privilege controls.

evidence_candidates.claim: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation identifies tool-mediated data exfiltration as a distinct threat path.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Adds a concrete exfiltration path for data protection and monitoring questions.

evidence_candidates.claim: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation identifies destructive impact through agent tools as a separate attack scenario.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Complements resilience, approval gates, rollback and incident response coverage.

evidence_candidates.claim: AI Telemetry Logging is an ATLAS mitigation relevant to recording agent and model activity for detection and investigation.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Candidate complement to observability, audit logging and incident response notes.

evidence_candidates.claim: Segmentation of AI Agent Components is an ATLAS mitigation for limiting propagation and blast radius across agent components.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Complements architecture, isolation and operational resilience controls.

evidence_candidates.claim: Input and Output Validation for AI Agent Components is an ATLAS mitigation addressing unsafe or manipulated data crossing agent component boundaries.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Complements prompt injection, RAG poisoning and tool response validation.

evidence_candidates.claim: AI Agent Authority Expansion Controls address increases in an agent's authority during operation.
evidence_candidates.relevance: High-value complement for authority boundaries, privileged actions and human approval.

evidence_candidates.claim: AI Agent Scope Drift Detection addresses divergence between the intended and observed scope of agent activity.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Candidate new concept for continuous governance and monitoring.

evidence_candidates.claim: ATLAS case studies include tool or MCP-based exfiltration, poisoned remote tools, compromise of AI infrastructure and multi-agent framework compromise.
evidence_candidates.relevance: Provides concrete threat scenarios to test coverage without treating incidents as legal requirements.

classification_proposals.basis: MITRE ATLAS threat-informed knowledge base; supports risk, control and scenario context, not binding obligations.
